## The BPA Lab

The **Business Process Automation Lab (BPA Lab)** is an ongoing project at **TH Köln (University of Applied Sciences)**, which supports research and teaching in the field of business process automation and analytics. It serves as a platform on which lecturers and students can study and extend selected concepts and technologies of business process automation and analytics.

As a *teaching* platform, the BPA Lab is used to support teaching in the field of business process automation and analysis. It offers students a tangible end-to-end scenario in which processes are modelled in BPMN and DMN, implemented in a BPMS, executed against physical hardware, and analysed using the resulting data. The didactic rationale and an early evaluation of this approach are documented in the project's first SoTL publication ([Chapter 6](chapter06-projects.qmd#sec-sotl-cos1326)).

As a *demonstration platform*, the BPA Lab provides an environment in which student projects, bachelor's and master's theses as well as smaller research projects can address questions around process automation and process analysis — for example regarding business process automation technologies, data architectures or process mining. The projects collected in [Chapter 6](chapter06-projects.qmd) illustrate the range of work that has been carried out on this basis.


## Conceptual overview

Beside the description of a fictional **business scenario**, this book also documents the **hardware and software aspects** of the BPA Lab and an overview of the **projects** conducted so far.

The lab combines **software components** (Business Process Management Systems, Robotic Process Automation, Process Mining) with **hardware components** (a Fischertechnik Industry 4.0 factory, a Fischertechnik warehouse robot, and IoT devices) to simulate the production and logistics processes of a bicycle manufacturer.

![BPA Lab — Conceptual Architecture](images/Conceptional_Architecture.png){#fig-concept fig-align="center"}

## About this book

This book aims to provide:

1. A **high-level overview** of the BPA Lab and its goals.
2. A **description of the business scenario** — the end-to-end ordering, manufacturing, and shipment process as currently implemented in the lab as well as additional (not-implemented)scenarios usable for teaching and research.
3. A **description of the software and system architecture** and the design decisions taken along the way.
4. A **collection of projects** that have been carried out using the BPA Lab.

It is structured as follows:

1. **Introduction:** Motivation, goals, and scope of the BPA Lab.
2. **Solution overview:** The three architectural layers — controllers, process applications, workflow engine.
3. **Business scenario:** The end-to-end bicycle ordering, manufacturing, and shipment process, broken down into its sub-processes (order management, production control, purchasing, manufacturing, shipment, warehouse operations).
4. **Data and data sources:** Data model, data flows, and persistence in the BPA Lab.
5. **Software architecture:** Requirements, a C4 view of the system, and the architecture decisions taken so far.
6. **Projects:** Research and teaching projects conducted using the BPA Lab.

The appendices contain:

- **Appendix A:** Overview of related components and related repositories.
- **Appendix B:** A glossary of key terms.
- **References:** All cited literature.

## Who this book is for

This book is documenting the current status of an ongoing project and therefore all work in progress. It is written for:

- **Students** working on bachelor's,  master's and other projects inside the BPA Lab.
- **Practitioners** looking for a concepts on combining a business process automation, IoT, and process mining.
- **Lecturers** who are interested in teaching business process automation and analytics with a tangible reference system.


## Source code and related repositories

The implementation of the demonstration factory is maintained as a separate repository: [bpa_lab_demonstration_factory](https://github.com/BpaLabTHCologne/bpa_lab_demonstration_factory).

Documentation for student component projects is available in the wiki of [bpa_lab_student_docs](https://github.com/BpaLabTHCologne/bpa_lab_student_docs/wiki).
